newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bangkok Investment, Thai Financial resume trading.
newsitem.headline: Bangkok Investment, Thai Financial resume trading.

text.p: The stock exchange of Thailand allowed shares of Thai finance and securities companies Bangkok Investment Plc and Thai Financial Syndicate Plc to resume trading from the afternoon session on Friday.
The exchange had halted the shares TRADING during the morning session suspecting that the two firms were planning a merger with Prime Finance and Securities Plc.
Prime was one of 16 financially distressed finance and securities companies ordered by the central bank to stop operations this morning as part of efforts to support the beleagured industry.

In a statement to the exchange Bangkok Investment said it had not entered into merger negotiations and would proceed with such discussions only with the approval of its largest shareholder, British bank Barclay's Plc.
In a further release Thai Financial Syndicate said it had not formally agreed to merge with Prime and two other brokers.
The Bank of Thailand and the Thai government is trying to bolster the stability of troubled Thai finance firms by encouraging consolidation among the 91 firms in the sector.

The Thai finance and securities industry is struggling to cope with declining revenues, high funding costs and a deterioratioon in asset quality amid Thailand's worst economic downturn for more than a decade.
